page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-64 is a general-purpose server powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The system is equipped with 256 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Cache specifications include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core processing capabilities, with stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU scores placing in the top 25% tier. Cryptographic and mathematical operations perform well, supported by hardware-accelerated instruction sets such as AES, VAES, SHA_NI, and FMA. Memory performance is highly efficient for cached workloads, achieving a read bandwidth of 4074.06 GB/sec, though uncached large-block memory transfers drop to average levels. Database operations are a notable strength, with Redis SET operations reaching 63.14 million operations per second.

While the server excels in multi-threaded CPU tasks and memory-cached operations, it exhibits limitations in large-scale model execution. Text generation using a large 70B LLM model falls into the bottom 10% tier at 2.41 tokens per second, reflecting the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration. This hardware profile is highly cost-efficient for general-purpose workloads requiring high CPU density and balanced memory without the premium of specialized accelerator hardware. It is well-suited for multi-threaded application hosting, database operations, web serving, and software compilation.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-64 is an x86_64 general-purpose server configured with 64 dedicated vCPUs and 256 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. This configuration provides a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core across 32 physical cores. The server lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage. Performance benchmarks show strong multi-core CPU execution, high-speed cached memory bandwidth, and excellent database throughput, with Redis SET operations reaching 63.14 million operations per second. However, large-scale LLM inference is a notable bottleneck, with 70B model text generation performing in the bottom 10%. This server represents a cost-efficient option for resource-dense general-purpose workloads, making it highly suitable for database hosting, multi-threaded application servers, web serving, and software compilation tasks.
